label: <DEL> step when the sequence starts with d/k/v/b/3/m/e/w
explanation: Fires almost only at the delimiter step: 96% of activation mass is at <DEL>, which is the step where the model has to output original token 0. Whether it fires there depends on which tokens it must recall first. It fires most when the first original token is in {d,k,v,b,3,m,e,w}; d is strongest, at about 60% of d-initial sequences. It fires more when the second token is also in that set (plus s and x), and more for longer sequences (L=8-9 carry most of the mass). It never fires during the original-input phase and only weakly and rarely during the copy phase, mostly just after <DEL>. The tendency looks graded, an additive preference over the first one or two tokens to be recalled, so a boolean predicate only gets F1 around 0.58 on dev. phase==1 alone has recall 0.92 but precision 0.12.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the token being output, by phase (delimiter step: d, k, v, b; copy phase: d, v, b, m; input phase: ) and the next token to output (most: d, v, k, s, 3, x; least: 2, g, j, 0); timing cues that raise it most: phase=1, recall_idx=0, L=3 & t=3.
